findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct Root cause §2: Popen(["true"]) succeeds on the sweep runner (the JUnit shows LockTimeout, not FileNotFoundError, and sibling tests using it are not deselected), so test_lock_stale_reclaim and test_stale_lock_reclaim_write fail only on `_pid_alive`; keep `dead_pid()` only as portability hygiene.

tests/unit/test_lock_stale_reclaim.py:79: test_acquire_does_not_reclaim_foreign_host_owner calls the same `_dead_pid()` (Popen(["true"])) and is NOT in any .github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args file.

For a legacy stamp `host:pid`, `_legacy_stamp_is_stale` returns `not _pid_alive(pid)`, which is always False on Windows today (lock_owner.py:289). That alone explains the LockTimeout.
findings.finding: The plan blames 2 failures on the `["true"]` helper, saying it 'does not exist on Windows'. The repo and the ticket's own evidence contradict that. Popen(["true"]) runs on the sweep runner, and these tests fail only because `_pid_alive` answers alive.
findings.location: Root cause §2, last bullet ('2 dead-pid helpers spawn ["true"], which does not exist on Windows')
scenarios: An implementer or later reader trusts the root-cause text and believes `dead_pid()` is what fixes test_lock_stale_reclaim and test_stale_lock_reclaim_write, when the `_windows_pid_alive` probe is what fixes them.
If the probe has a defect, these 2 tests are still expected to pass because 'the helper was fixed', which hides the real regression.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the last bullet of Root cause §2 along these lines: 'The 4 `Popen(["true"])` dead-pid helpers depend on a POSIX `true` on PATH. It happens to exist on the windows-latest runner, so they are not a cause of these failures; test_lock_stale_reclaim and test_stale_lock_reclaim_write fail only because the legacy-stamp reclaim reads `not _pid_alive(pid)`. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `dead_pid()` keep the reaped Popen object referenced for the test's lifetime (e.g. via a fixture or a module-level list) so its handle pins the pid against reuse on Windows.
evidence: '`dead_pid()` ... spawn `[sys.executable, "-c", ""]` and reap it.'
Decision table: a reused pid either opens (wait times out → alive) or fails with 5 (→ alive).
findings.finding: `dead_pid()` spawns and reaps a child, then returns only the pid. On Windows the Popen object, and with it the process handle, is released when the helper returns. Windows recycles pids aggressively. Under xdist with many spawning workers the 'dead' pid can be reassigned before the test probes it, and then it reads alive.
scenarios: A Windows sweep worker gets the pid of a reaped child. Another worker's process takes over that pid, so the stale-reclaim test sees a live owner and fails intermittently.
findings.suggested_fix: Turn `dead_pid` into a pytest fixture, or have it return `(proc, pid)` with callers holding `proc`. While the handle is open, OpenProcess succeeds and WaitForSingleObject returns WAIT_OBJECT_0, giving a deterministic 'dead' verdict.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make dead_pid() keep the reaped Popen (and therefore its process handle) referenced for the test's lifetime, so the pid cannot be recycled before it is probed; do the same in the Windows-only real-probe test.
evidence: "dead_pid() replaces the 4 Popen([\"true\"]) copies ... spawn [sys.executable, \"-c\", \"\"] and reap it."
"On Windows only, a real spawned-and-reaped child reads dead"
Windows platform fact: a process's pid is released for reuse when its last handle closes, and reuse can be prompt.
findings.finding: dead_pid() spawns `[sys.executable, "-c", ""]`, reaps it, and returns only its pid. On Windows a pid becomes reusable once the last handle to the process object closes. The Popen handle closes when the returned-from helper's Popen is garbage-collected. Windows recycles freed pids quickly, and xdist workers on a busy runner spawn many processes. The 'dead' pid can therefore belong to a new live process by the time the test stamps and probes it. The probe then answers alive and the test fails intermittently. The same Windows-only real test ('a real spawned-and-reaped child reads dead') is exposed in the same way if it drops its Popen before probing.
scenarios: The Windows sweep under xdist: dead_pid() returns pid P and the Popen is collected. A sibling worker's subprocess receives P. test_lock_stale_reclaim then stamps P, the probe opens a live process, the lock is not reclaimed, and the test fails intermittently. That keeps the line in pid-liveness.args or re-adds it later.
findings.suggested_fix: Have dead_pid() append the reaped Popen to a module-level list, or return it alongside the pid, or expose it as a fixture that holds the Popen until teardown. While that handle is open the pid stays reserved, and the probe answers dead via WaitForSingleObject returning WAIT_OBJECT_0.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `dead_pid()` keep the reaped Popen (its process handle) alive for the test's lifetime on Windows, so the pid stays reserved and reads dead via WaitForSingleObject instead of relying on the pid not being reused.
evidence: Plan: "`dead_pid()` ... spawn `[sys.executable, "-c", ""]` and reap it." It returns only the pid.
Plan: "`stop(proc, pid)` ... polls `lock_owner._pid_alive(pid)` until False, bounded at 30 s with a failure if it is still alive."
sweep-windows runs `pytest ... -n 4 --dist worksteal` (test.yml:281-282).
findings.finding: Windows reuses freed pids from a free list and tends to hand them out again soon. The new helpers assume a pid stays unused once its process is gone. dead_pid() spawns and reaps a child and returns only the int pid, so the Popen, and with it the last handle keeping the pid reserved, is dropped. Under `-n 4 --dist worksteal`, with many subprocesses starting, another process can take that pid before the test reads the stamp. The pid then reads alive and the dead-owner test fails at random. stop() has the same exposure while it polls `_pid_alive(pid)` for up to 30 s. On POSIX pids are allocated in increasing order, so this hardly ever happens there, which is why the existing `test_stamped_lock` form has looked safe.
scenarios: test_lock_stale_reclaim gets a dead pid. Before the lock is checked, an xdist worker's git subprocess takes the same pid, the stamp reads alive, nothing is reclaimed, and the test fails at random on Windows.
findings.suggested_fix: Have dead_pid() keep the waited Popen in a module-level list, or return it to a fixture that holds it until teardown. While that handle is open, Windows cannot reuse the pid, and the new probe proves the process exited through WAIT_OBJECT_0. POSIX behaviour is unchanged.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that OpenProcess is called with SYNCHRONIZE (0x00100000) access and bInheritHandle=False, and have the fake-kernel32 test assert the access mask passed.
evidence: 'The real path uses `ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)` with explicit argtypes/restype' — no dwDesiredAccess value given
'Any other wait result: alive (True).'
findings.finding: The plan does not state the access mask passed to OpenProcess. WaitForSingleObject needs SYNCHRONIZE access on the handle. A handle opened with only PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION makes the wait return WAIT_FAILED. That maps to 'alive' under the decision table, so the probe would silently never report an exited-but-still-referenced process as dead.
scenarios: The executor picks PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, a common least-privilege choice. Every reaped child still referenced by a handle reads alive, and test_stamped_lock and test_write_lock_busy_probe_7084 still fail on Windows.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the decision table: 'OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE, False, pid); a NULL handle means failure, read via get_last_error().' Add a fake-kernel32 assertion on the first OpenProcess argument.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile Testing and AC1: state whether AC1 needs the whole job green or only the removed tests passing, and which later scheduled run counts if the first one fails for an unrelated reason.
evidence: Testing: 'the first scheduled `test.yml` run on main ... Its `sweep (windows)` job must pass with the lines removed.'
AC1: 'Every line removed ... names a test that passed in a `sweep (windows)` run on main after the fix'

AC1 only requires that each removed line's test passed in some post-fix main run. Neither says what happens if that first scheduled run fails, for an unrelated deselect file or a flake.
findings.location: Testing 'AC1 evidence' paragraph vs Acceptance Criteria AC1
scenarios: The first scheduled run fails on a test from a different .args class. The executor cannot tell whether AC1 is met (all removed tests passed) or blocked (the job failed, so wait for the next scheduled run).
findings.suggested_fix: State a default: 'AC1 is met by the earliest scheduled main run containing the merge commit in which every removed test passed (per-test outcomes from its JUnit). Unrelated failures in that job do not block, but are noted in the comment.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a back-out note: if the post-merge Windows sweep fails or a false-dead reclaim is reported, revert the lock_owner/compact_trigger change and restore the affected pid-liveness.args lines in the same revert.
evidence: 'a dead same-host owner is now provably stale and is reclaimed, as on POSIX'
'hidden staging of a dead same-host owner is now removed at once instead of after the age ceiling'
No rollback or back-out text anywhere in the plan; 'No config key, env var or flag.'

The plan gives no back-out if the probe misreads a live owner as dead in the field, or if a removed test fails on main after merge. No step says whether to revert the commit, restore the args lines, or both.

scenarios: A false 'dead' verdict on Windows reclaims a live writer's lock or removes its staging. Or the scheduled main sweep fails on an un-deselected test, and nothing says what to do.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State what happens to a line whose test still fails in validation: fix it within this ticket, or move it to a new ticket's args file with a recorded reason.
evidence: 'A line leaves the args file only if its test passed there.'
AC2: '... or each remaining line names a test recorded on this ticket as intentionally unsupported on Windows with the reason.'
findings.finding: No step covers a test that still fails in the pre-merge Windows validation. AC2's escape only allows lines 'intentionally unsupported on Windows with the reason'. That does not fit a test still broken by a fixable defect, for example one the plan's two root causes do not explain.
scenarios: test_mcp_idle_sync still fails on Windows for a reason other than the pid mismatch. Its line stays, but it is not 'intentionally unsupported', so neither AC branch can be satisfied.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Log the exception once (e.g. logger.debug/warning on first failure) in the `_windows_pid_alive` catch-all, and cover it in the fake-kernel32 exception-path test.
evidence: 'Any exception (no ctypes, missing symbol): alive (True).'
No logging or warning is mentioned for the fallback.
findings.finding: `_windows_pid_alive` swallows every exception and answers 'alive' without logging. If ctypes or a kernel32 symbol is unavailable, or argtypes are wrong, Windows silently reverts to today's behaviour: dead locks are reclaimed only by the age ceiling. Nothing would let an operator see that the probe is degraded.
findings.location: Approach — decision table, 'Any exception (no ctypes, missing symbol): alive (True).'
scenarios: A packaging or embedded-Python build lacks ctypes. Stale locks wait for the age ceiling on every run, and nothing explains why.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in the plan that _windows_pid_alive calls OpenProcess with SYNCHRONIZE (optionally plus PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION), and have the fake-kernel32 test assert the access mask it receives.
evidence: "The real path uses ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True) with explicit argtypes/restype" — no access rights named
"WaitForSingleObject(h, 0) == WAIT_OBJECT_0: exited (False). Any other wait result: alive (True)."
The fake-kernel32 table injects OpenProcess/Wait results, so it is agnostic to the access mask passed.
findings.finding: The plan never states the dwDesiredAccess mask passed to OpenProcess. WaitForSingleObject on a process handle requires SYNCHRONIZE access. If the implementation opens the process with only PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION or PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION, which is common for liveness probes, the wait returns WAIT_FAILED. Under the stated table every WAIT_FAILED maps to alive. Exited-but-still-referenced processes would then never read dead. Only a pid whose process object is gone (OpenProcess error 87) would read dead. So the fix would work only partially, and the fake-kernel32 table cannot detect this.
scenarios: Windows: an exited holder whose process object is still referenced (for example by a parent's Popen handle) is opened without SYNCHRONIZE. WaitForSingleObject returns WAIT_FAILED (error 5), the probe returns alive, and the stale lock is never reclaimed — the bug this plan targets.
findings.suggested_fix: State: `h = OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE | PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, False, pid)` (SYNCHRONIZE = 0x00100000, PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION = 0x1000). Add a decision-table case asserting that the fake OpenProcess was called with SYNCHRONIZE set.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the pre-merge validation tree drop all 14 pid-liveness.args lines (or the whole file and its test.yml @ line) before dispatch, so the deselected tests actually run; then restore only the lines whose tests failed.
evidence: .github/workflows/test.yml:289: `'@.github/windows-sweep-deselect/pid-liveness.args'` is passed to the sweep-windows pytest command.
pid-liveness.args lines 1-14 are all `--deselect=<nodeid>` for exactly the tests the plan wants to validate.
Plan: 'push the exact tree to tmp/b4-smoking-bereft-boar ... record the run id and per-test outcomes ... A line leaves the args file only if its test passed there.'
findings.finding: The plan assumes the pre-merge Windows validation run will produce per-test outcomes for the 14 tests. It will not, because the pushed tree still deselects them. The plan pushes 'the exact tree' and removes a line only after its test passes there, so that tree still has the 14 `--deselect` lines. The sweep-windows command passes the file to pytest, so none of the 14 tests runs and none can pass. The removal step depends on a result that can never exist.
findings.location: Testing → 'Pre-merge Windows validation' bullet; Approach → '.github/windows-sweep-deselect/pid-liveness.args: remove each line whose test passes in the Windows validation run'
scenarios: The implementer dispatches the tmp branch with the args file unchanged. All 14 tests are deselected, the JUnit has no entries for them, and no line can ever qualify for removal.
Alternatively, the implementer removes lines before any validation and drops the 'only if it passed there' gate in practice.
findings.suggested_fix: In Testing, say that the tmp-branch tree is the candidate final tree with pid-liveness.args emptied.
